title: Ask, answer, and repair misunderstandings
lessons:
# Chapter 3 — Ask, answer, and repair misunderstandings

## Goals and starting point
Build on the greetings and personal facts from Chapters 1–2. This chapter makes interaction possible when you need information or miss a word. You will form questions, use common negative patterns, spell or confirm details, and ask for clarification. If a question feels intimidating, begin with a statement and raise your voice slightly; that is a common conversational question pattern.

## Three useful question patterns
A simple statement can become a spoken yes/no question through intonation: `Vous habitez ici ?` (Do you live here?). Another familiar pattern puts **est-ce que** before a statement: `Est-ce que vous habitez ici ?` The spelling keeps est-ce que together as a chunk. More formal inversion places the verb before the subject: `Habitez-vous ici ?` Recognize it, but focus on the first two patterns for comfortable everyday speech.

Question words usually appear at the start: `où` (where), `quand` (when), `comment` (how), `pourquoi` (why), `qui` (who), `quel/quelle` (which/what, agreeing with a noun), and `combien` (how much/how many). Examples: `Où est l'arrêt ?` (Where is the stop?) and `À quelle heure le magasin ouvre ?` (At what time does the shop open?). The question word should match the information you need; do not translate an English question word mechanically.

## Negation and clarification
In careful writing, place `ne` before the conjugated verb and `pas` after it: `Je ne sais pas` (I don't know). In everyday speech, **ne** is often dropped (`Je sais pas`), but learn the complete form first and keep it in writing or formal speech. With infinitives, place the pair before the infinitive: `ne pas oublier` (not to forget). Common variants include `ne...plus` (no longer/not anymore), `ne...jamais` (never), and `ne...rien` (nothing). For nouns, `Je n'ai pas de question` uses **de** after negation rather than **une/des**.

Repair phrases are communication tools, not failures: `Pardon ?`, `Vous pouvez répéter ?`, `Comment ça s'écrit ?` (How is that spelled?), and `Qu'est-ce que vous voulez dire ?` (What do you mean?). To verify, repeat what you heard: `Vous avez dit mardi ?` (You said Tuesday?). Keep the tone curious and polite. If you miss only one detail, ask a narrow question instead of requesting the whole message again.

## Listening and literacy
Listen once for the situation, a second time for the requested detail. On reading, watch for question marks and question words, but do not rely on punctuation alone: word order and context matter. For speaking, ask one open and one confirmation question. For writing, compose a short, courteous information request with one clear question.

## Cumulative retrieval
Attempt from memory; then open the blocks and say each French phrase.

Before the first reveal: From memory, ask where, when, and how using French question words, then say “I don't know” as a complete negative sentence.

:::answer
`Où` asks where; `quand` asks when; `comment` asks how. A written negative often has `ne` before and `pas` after the conjugated verb: `Je ne sais pas`.
:::

Before the second reveal: Ask in French how a name is spelled, then confirm that someone said Tuesday.

:::answer
To ask for spelling, say `Comment ça s'écrit ?` To check a day you heard, say `Vous avez dit mardi ?` In casual speech you may hear `Je sais pas`, but include ne in careful writing.
:::

## Self-check and review
Can you ask where, when, and how? Can you form a polite repair request? Can you turn a positive sentence into ne...pas without moving the verb? Review 12 bank items after one day, three days, and one week. Log the question type or negative pattern that caused hesitation. Reuse that form in a new question rather than simply rereading its explanation.

bank.cue: The first word asks about time.

bank.prompt: Ask how someone is doing politely.

bank.fr: Pourquoi le bus est-il en retard ?

bank.cue: The person sought is the subject.

bank.en: Which book are you looking for?
bank.prompt: Identify the object being asked about.

bank.en: How much does this ticket cost?
bank.prompt: Ask the price of a ticket.

bank.fr: Est-ce que vous avez une réservation ?

bank.prompt: Turn this statement into a spoken yes/no question using intonation.
bank.cue: Raise your voice at the end.

bank.prompt: Ask a friend where they live.
bank.cue: Put the place question word first.

bank.en: At what time are you leaving?
bank.prompt: Extract the kind of detail requested.
bank.cue: The question asks for departure time.

bank.en: Since when have you worked here?
bank.cue: Depuis quand asks from what time.

bank.prompt: Say you do not know in careful French.

bank.fr: Je ne comprends pas la question.
bank.prompt: Explain what you do not understand.

bank.fr: Elle ne travaille pas le lundi.
bank.cue: Place ne before travaille and pas after it.

bank.fr: Nous ne sommes pas en retard.

bank.cue: Une becomes de after the negative.

bank.fr: Je ne prends jamais le métro.

bank.prompt: Understand the change in her workplace.
bank.cue: Plus means no longer in this negative.

bank.en: We don't want to order anything.

bank.fr: Je ne peux pas venir demain.

bank.cue: A negative command begins with n'.

bank.fr: Il ne faut pas courir ici.
Je n'ai pas entendu le dernier mot.
bank.en: I didn't hear the last word.
Are you talking about room B?
bank.cue: De la salle names the topic.
Repeat the candidate day as a question.

bank.prompt: Ask someone to spell a word.
bank.cue: S'écrit is written with an accent.

bank.prompt: Ask a speaker to slow down naturally.

bank.fr: Un peu plus fort, s'il vous plaît.

bank.en: I'm going to check the address.
bank.prompt: Hear what the speaker will check.
Ask for confirmation of a number.

bank.en: I confirm: it is indeed Tuesday.
bank.cue: Bien reinforces that Tuesday is correct.

bank.fr: Vous voulez dire le bâtiment neuf ?
bank.en: Do you mean the new building?

bank.fr: Non, je parle du bâtiment nord.
bank.en: No, I'm talking about the north building.
I'm looking for the main entrance.

bank.fr: L'entrée n'est pas de ce côté.
bank.en: The entrance isn't on this side.

bank.prompt: Check the distance from your location.

bank.fr: Non, ce n'est qu'à deux minutes.
bank.en: No, it's only two minutes away.
bank.prompt: Understand how long the walk is.

bank.en: Do I need to make an appointment?
bank.prompt: Ask whether an appointment is necessary.
bank.cue: Faut-il asks whether it is necessary.

bank.en: You must fill in this form.
bank.prompt: Identify what the person must do.
Ask where a signature is required.
bank.cue: Dois-je is inversion of devoir and je.

bank.fr: Signez en bas de la page.
bank.en: Sign at the bottom of the page.
bank.cue: En bas means at the bottom.

bank.fr: Je ne trouve pas la ligne.
bank.prompt: Explain the problem with a form.

bank.en: Which line should I fill in?

bank.fr: Je voudrais savoir si c'est ouvert.
bank.en: I'd like to know whether it's open.

bank.fr: Savez-vous à quelle heure ça ferme ?
bank.en: Do you know what time it closes?
bank.cue: The question asks the closing hour.

bank.fr: Je ne suis pas certain de l'heure.
bank.en: I'm not sure of the time.
bank.cue: Certain has a feminine spelling variant.

bank.fr: Pouvez-vous me montrer sur le plan ?
bank.en: Could you show me on the map?

bank.fr: Je ne vois pas le nom de la rue.
bank.en: I can't see the street name.
bank.prompt: Identify what is hard to see.

bank.fr: La rue est indiquée en bleu.
bank.en: The street is marked in blue.
bank.prompt: Hear how the street is marked.

bank.cue: L' stands for the thing to write.

bank.en: I'll write it on this paper.
bank.cue: Sur ce papier means on this paper.

bank.fr: Je ne lis pas bien cette écriture.
bank.en: I can't read this handwriting well.
Could you write in capital letters?

bank.fr: Le nom commence par un B.
bank.en: The name begins with a B.

bank.fr: Il se termine par un accent.
bank.en: It ends with an accent mark.
bank.cue: Se termine par means ends with.

bank.fr: Est-ce un accent aigu ou grave ?
bank.en: Is it an acute or grave accent?
bank.prompt: Ask which accent mark is used.
bank.cue: Aigu and grave name the marks.

bank.fr: C'est un accent aigu sur le e.
bank.en: It's an acute accent on the e.

bank.fr: Je ne connais pas ce prénom.
bank.en: I don't know this first name.
bank.cue: Connaître means know a person or thing.

bank.en: How do you pronounce this name?
bank.prompt: Ask how to pronounce a name.
Understand which letter at the end of a word is pronounced.

bank.fr: Le h ne se prononce pas ici.
bank.en: The h is not pronounced here.

bank.fr: Je peux essayer encore une fois ?
bank.en: Can I try one more time?
bank.cue: Encore une fois means one more time.
Prenez votre temps is the reassurance.

bank.fr: Je suis désolé de vous interrompre.

bank.cue: Poser une question is the verb phrase.

bank.en: I'd like to clarify one detail.

bank.fr: Est-ce que vous parlez de demain matin ?
bank.en: Are you talking about tomorrow morning?
bank.cue: The proposed time is tomorrow morning.

bank.fr: Non, je voulais dire vendredi soir.
bank.cue: Je voulais dire means I meant.

bank.fr: Je n'ai pas compris la dernière phrase.
bank.en: I didn't understand the last sentence.

bank.prompt: Understand how an explanation will continue.
bank.cue: Donner un exemple is give an example.

bank.fr: Je ne suis toujours pas sûr.

bank.en: I'm missing one piece of information.
bank.prompt: State that one detail is still missing.
bank.cue: Il me manque expresses something missing.

bank.fr: Vous n'avez rien à signer aujourd'hui.
bank.en: You have nothing to sign today.
bank.prompt: Understand what is not required today.
bank.cue: Rien à signer means nothing to sign.

bank.en: Do we need to wait here?
bank.prompt: Ask whether waiting here is necessary.

bank.en: No, you can come in now.
I'm not waiting for anyone else.

bank.fr: Vous avez bien reçu mon message ?
bank.en: Did you receive my message okay?

bank.fr: Je n'ai pas encore reçu de réponse.
bank.en: I haven't received a reply yet.

bank.fr: Merci d'avoir pris le temps de répondre.
bank.en: Thank you for taking the time to answer.
bank.cue: Prendre le temps means take the time.

activities.title: Clarify an appointment
activities.prompt: Listen to the full exchange. What is the confirmed appointment day and time?
activities.script: — Bonjour, je voudrais confirmer mon rendez-vous. Est-ce que c'est jeudi à neuf heures ? — Non, vous avez dit jeudi, mais l'heure est neuf heures et demie. — Pardon, vous pouvez répéter ? — Neuf heures trente, à la clinique du centre.
activities.explanation: The speaker confirms Thursday but corrects the time to neuf heures et demie, or 9:30.

activities.title: Ask for a spelling
activities.prompt: Listen for the spelling detail. Which letter ends the family name?
activities.script: — Votre nom de famille, s'il vous plaît ? — Beaulieu. — Pardon, comment ça s'écrit ? — B-E-A-U-L-I-E-U. Le dernier son est comme dans « lieu ».
activities.explanation: The spelling ends with U: B-E-A-U-L-I-E-U.

activities.title: Read a clinic instruction
activities.prompt: Read the instructions. What should a visitor do first?
activities.passage: Rendez-vous à 14 h. Présentez-vous à l'accueil dix minutes avant. Si vous ne trouvez pas la salle 208, demandez de l'aide au personnel. Il n'est pas nécessaire d'apporter une copie du formulaire.
activities.explanation: The note asks visitors to report to reception ten minutes before a 14:00 appointment.

activities.title: Understand a message thread
activities.prompt: Read the exchange and determine what is still unknown.
activities.passage: Nora : Tu viens à la réunion demain ? Karim : Oui, mais je ne sais pas où elle a lieu. Nora : Au centre communautaire, salle 4. Karim : Merci ! À quelle heure ? Nora : Je vérifie et je te réponds.
activities.explanation: Nora gives the location and room, but says she will check and reply about the time.

activities.title: Get the missing information
activities.prompt: Role-play calling a community centre. Ask when a beginner class starts, confirm the location, and request repetition of one detail. Continue for about 35 seconds; invent plausible details only for your role-play.
activities.model: Bonjour, je vous appelle au sujet du cours de français. À quelle heure commence-t-il ? Est-ce qu'il a lieu au centre du quartier ? Pardon, vous pouvez répéter l'heure, s'il vous plaît ? Merci, j'ai compris.
rubric: I asked clear questions using a question word or est-ce que.
I used a polite repair or confirmation phrase.
I responded to the information instead of listing unrelated questions.

activities.title: Request clarification by email
activities.prompt: Write a 45–65-word polite email to an office. Say that you received an appointment notice but do not understand the room number; ask them to confirm the room and whether you should arrive early.
activities.model: Bonjour, j'ai reçu votre avis de rendez-vous pour mardi, mais je ne comprends pas le numéro de la salle. Pourriez-vous me le confirmer, s'il vous plaît ? Dois-je arriver quelques minutes à l'avance ? Merci de votre aide. Je vous remercie de votre réponse rapide. Cordialement, Amira
rubric: The email explains the source of confusion.
It asks two focused questions politely.
The greeting and closing suit a formal message.
